Name: Poke ball Collection
Author: Lucidvisionsinc
Description:
[center][size=6][b]Poké Ball Collection[/b][/size]

Bring Pokémon-inspired Poké Balls to Stardew Valley! Grow Apricorn trees, craft modern and Hisuian-style Poké Balls, discover unique collectibles, and take your collection into combat with [b]21 throwable Poké Ball weapons[/b].[/center]

From cultivating colorful Apricorns to using specialized crafting machines and battling monsters with distinctive projectiles, Poké Ball Collection adds new items, crafting, shops, events, and combat feedback to your valley.

[b]Please note:[/b] Poké Ball weapons can damage and defeat monsters, but this mod does not implement a functional Pokémon or monster capture system.

[b]________________________________________[/b]

[size=5][b]🌱 Grow Apricorns[/b][/size]

Plant Apricorn saplings and grow trees that produce eight varieties of Apricorns:

[list]
[*]Brown[/*]
[*]Black[/*]
[*]Blue[/*]
[*]Green[/*]
[*]Pink[/*]
[*]Red[/*]
[*]White[/*]
[*]Yellow[/*]
[/list]
These fruit trees take 28 days to mature and bear fruit in spring, summer, and fall. Seven sapling colors are sold by merchants around the valley and in the desert. Brown Apricorn Saplings are available from the Traveling Cart.

[b]________________________________________[/b]

[size=5][b]⚙️ Apricorn Forge[/b][/size]

Turn your harvest into Poké Balls with the Apricorn Forge. Craft it after reaching [b]Farming level 6[/b], using:

[list]
[*]10 Copper Bars[/*]
[*]5 Iron Bars[/*]
[*]1 Iridium Bar[/*]
[/list]
Robin also sells the machine for [b]8,000g[/b].

Place one colored Apricorn into the forge to produce its corresponding Poké Ball. Each processing cycle takes [b]two hours[/b].

[size=5][b]🏺 Ancient Hisui Forge[/b][/size]

The Ancient Hisui Forge offers another approach to crafting, inspired by the traditional Poké Ball designs of Hisui.

Sandy sells the forge for [b]12,000g[/b]. The Dwarf also sells it for [b]10,000g[/b] after you reach [b]750 friendship points with the Dwarf[/b] and receive the Adventurer's Guild membership mail.

Each cycle takes [b]two hours[/b] and consumes the Brown Apricorn and selected material. If you carry more than one eligible material, the forge checks Stone first, followed by Wood, Hardwood, and Coal. If you have none of those materials, it rejects the Apricorn without consuming it.

[b]________________________________________[/b]

[size=5][b]🎒 Collect, Keep, and Throw[/b][/size]

Poké Ball Collection separates collectible Poké Ball items from their throwable weapon counterparts. Using a supported Poké Ball item grants its matching weapon once; the helper's conversion action does not consume the original item. This conversion requires SpaceCore.

Poké Ball objects are decor-category collectibles that can also be gifted or sold. They are not weapons themselves. Equip a weapon version to attack monsters.

The collection includes familiar designs, specialty balls, rare variants, and Hisuian-style Poké Balls. Items come from machine crafting, shops, and special events.

[b]________________________________________[/b]

[b]Stat notes:[/b] Precision uses Stardew Valley's [b]0–10 scale[/b] (corrected in version 1.0.1). Critical-hit chance is the raw decimal configured by the mod, not a percentage conversion. Knockback is Stardew's multiplier relative to a base weapon. AoE is the game's weapon area-of-effect value. Weapon speed is distinct from projectile velocity; the mod omits the weapon Speed field, so these weapons use the data default of 0 (no weapon speed bonus).

[b]¹Projectile damage note:[/b] The projectile-damage values in the data are listed for completeness. For these mod weapons, the helper stores the source weapon's damage range and relevant combat stats on the projectile and supplies them when it hits. Thus, the projectile's configured damage number is not the effective weapon damage range. Applicable player combat buffs are included, and Stardew Valley's normal damage calculations still apply. Every projectile is configured to explode, has a 20-tile maximum travel distance, and uses its listed sprite index from the modded projectile sheet. Projectile angle offsets vary by weapon; most are between 0 and 2 degrees, with the standard Poké Ball between 1 and 3 degrees.

[b]________________________________________[/b]

[size=5][b]❤️ Temporary Monster Health Bars[/b][/size]

After a supported Poké Ball weapon slash or projectile damages a monster, a temporary health bar appears above it. It reflects the monster's actual current and maximum health, changes from green through yellow to red as health falls, refreshes when another qualifying hit reduces health, and fades after approximately two seconds without another qualifying hit. It is removed when the monster dies, is removed from the location, or leaves the active encounter.

[b]________________________________________[/b]

[size=5][b]✨ Capture-Inspired Combat Effects[/b][/size]

[list]
[*]Poké Ball projectile throwing, bounce, and impact sounds.[/*]
[*]A capture-inspired sound when a supported weapon defeats a monster.[/*]
[*]Pale-blue sparkle particles and a fade effect for supported defeats, based on Stardew Valley's ghost visuals.[/*]
[*]Projectile sprites can be enabled or disabled with the Content Patcher config option
[code]PokeballProjectiles[/code](enabled by default).[/*]
[/list]
The effect code suppresses selected vanilla death visuals and known splat or chunk sprites while processing supported attacks. It cannot guarantee suppression for every vanilla or custom monster implementation. Flying Serpents retain their native disappearance behavior instead of receiving the generic capture fade.

[b]________________________________________[/b]

[size=5][b]🌟 Poké Ball Collection and Acquisition[/b][/size]

The collection includes standard Poké Balls, Apricorn balls, specialty variants, the GS Ball, Master Ball, Infinity Master Ball, and four Hisui-style variants.

[list]
[*][b]Pierre's General Store:[/b] Poké Ball, Great Ball, Premier Ball, and Fast Ball.[/*]
[*][b]Desert Trader:[/b] Poké Ball, Great Ball, and Ultra Ball (requires Mining level 5); Master Ball after receiving the Adventurer's Guild membership mail.[/*]
[*][b]The Dwarf:[/b] Heavy Ball, Level Ball, and Moon Ball; Master Ball and Ancient Hisui Forge after 750 friendship points with the Dwarf and the guild membership mail.[/*]
[*][b]Krobus:[/b] Love Ball, Friend Ball, and Heal Ball; Master Ball after 750 friendship points with Krobus and the guild membership mail.[/*]
[*][b]Sandy:[/b] Dive Ball, Lure Ball, Net Ball, and the Ancient Hisui Forge.[/*]
[*][b]Traveling Cart:[/b] GS Ball and Brown Apricorn Sapling.[/*]
[*][b]Adventurer's Guild:[/b] Throwable weapon versions of Poké Ball, Great Ball, Ultra Ball, Premier Ball, Heavy Ball, Fast Ball, Friend Ball, Love Ball, Net Ball, Dive Ball, Lure Ball, Moon Ball, Level Ball, and Heal Ball.[/*]
[*][b]Robin's Carpenter Shop:[/b] Apricorn Forge and seven non-brown Apricorn saplings.[/*]
[/list]
Seven non-brown sapling colors are also sold at Pierre's, the Dwarf, Krobus, Sandy, and the Desert Trader. The Brown Apricorn Sapling and GS Ball have limited stock at the Traveling Cart.

[size=4][b]Infinity Master Ball[/b][/size]

At the Volcano Forge, combine a Master Ball with an item carrying Stardew Valley's
[code]color_prismatic[/code]context tag and pay [b]20 Cinder Shards[/b] to make an Infinity Master Ball. The game checks the tag, so the eligible item is not limited to a single named item.

[b]________________________________________[/b]

[size=5][b]🎉 Special Events[/b][/size]

[list]
[*][b]Linus's Premier Ball event:[/b] The Mountain event requires the 6:00–26:00 time condition, at least 750 friendship points with Linus, and that the event has not already been seen. Linus gives one Premier Ball.[/*]
[*][b]GS Ball dream event:[/b] A one-time FarmHouse dream sequence that requires the GS Ball in the player's inventory. The event is associated with the GS Ball; it does not give the ball.[/*]
[/list]
[b]________________________________________[/b]

[size=5][b]📖 Optional Poké Ball Collector's Guide[/b][/size]

The optional Poké Ball Collector's Guide add-on uses Parchment Core to provide an in-game reference covering Apricorn trees, both machines, their recipes, shop sources, and the collection. It is a separate Content Patcher pack and is not required for the main mod.

[b]________________________________________[/b]

[size=5][b]📦 Installation[/b][/size]

[list=1]
[*]Install SMAPI and the required dependencies listed below.[/*]
[*]Download and extract the main mod. Install both the [b]Poké Ball Items Helper[/b] SMAPI folder and the [b]Poké Ball content pack[/b] Content Patcher folder into
[code]Stardew Valley/Mods[/code], preserving their folder structure.[/*]
[*]Launch Stardew Valley through SMAPI and check the console for missing dependencies or loading errors.[/*]
[*]To use the optional guide, install its separate Content Patcher folder and Parchment Core.[/*]
[/list]
[size=4][b]Requirements[/b][/size]

[b]Main mod[/b]

[list]
[*]Stardew Valley[/*]
[*]SMAPI 4.0.0 or later[/*]
[*]Content Patcher[/*]
[*]SpaceCore[/*]
[*]Poké Ball Items Helper SMAPI component[/*]
[/list]
The Content Patcher pack requires SpaceCore and the helper component. The helper component itself requires SpaceCore.

[b]Optional guidebook[/b]

[list]
[*]Parchment Core 1.12.1 or later[/*]
[*]The main Poké Ball Content Patcher pack[/*]
[/list]
